newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia rupiah stable, swaps fall after rate cut.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia rupiah stable, swaps fall after rate cut.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah was stable against the dollar in slow late trading on Thursday, but swap rates were seen falling, dealers said.
They said expectations of ample liquidity on Friday, coupled with the central bank discount rates cut of 50 basis points on Thursday seemed to have dragged swap rates down.

One local bank dealer said sentiment on dollars seemed to improve following narrowing interest rate differentials between the dollar and the rupiah, but fears over tightening liquidity due to year-end factors capped the upside.
However, operators seemed to anticipate flush liquidity on Friday despite weekly tax payments.
"We don't think weekly tax payments could net off rupiah injection induced by central bank dollar buying on Wednesday," the local bank dealer said.
Bank Indonesia was speculated to have bought at least $500 million from the market to keep the dollar within the band.
Spot rupiah closed at 2,348.4/48.6 in Jakarta against an opening of 2,347.5/48.5. Tomorrow and today rupiah closed at 2,347.0/47.5 and 2,345.75/46.25, respectively.
Bank Indonesia raised its intervention band by one point to 2,347/2,539 and the conversion band to 2,347/2,395.
Dealers said the hike was anticipated.
Overnight swap fell to 0.35/0.45 from 0.4/0.5. Tom/next dropped to 0.9/1.1 from 1.5/1.6 points.
"This seems to signal ample condition on Friday," one dealer said.
Bank Indonesia cut its key discount rate for short-term securities (SBPUs) by 50 basis points for all maturities.
One-week SBPU fell to 15.25 percent, two to 15.50 percent, one-, three-, six- and 12-month to 16.0 percent. Dealers said SBI rates were also seen down 25 basis points from Wednesday.
Dealers said operators seemed to have discounted the move although it surprised the market when it happened.
Some economists said the cut suggested that the overheated economy was on the way to cooling down following lower inflation and a slowdown in monetary growth.
One-month swaps declined to 14.5/15.2 from 15.00/15.75, two to 29.5/30.5 from 30.0/31.5, three to 42.0/43.0 from 42.5/43.25 and six to 85.0/86.0 from 86.0/87.0.
